title: gateway-identity.v1 — the signed identity the gateway forwards to the services behind it
description: The gateway resolves a bearer through identity's /internal/validate and forwards the request with X-Vexa-Identity: "v1." + base64url(claims JSON) + "." + base64url(Ed25519 signature, by the gateway's private key, over "v1." + base64url(claims JSON)). "v1" fixes the scheme; nothing is negotiated. agent-api, meeting-api and the credential broker hold only the gateway's public key, so they verify and cannot sign: the signature, then the issue time and the expiry within a bounded clock skew. agent-api and meeting-api rebuild every x-user-* header from these claims and refuse with 401 a request that asserts an x-user-* header without a valid signature and without the internal tier's X-Internal-Secret. The credential broker refuses an agent-role call whose forwarded signature is missing, invalid or names a subject other than the assertion's actor.

sub.description: the user id identity resolved; becomes x-user-id

email.description: the verified email identity holds; becomes x-user-email

exp.description: expires at, unix seconds; a verifier refuses exp - iat > 300

Delegation.description: Present when the bearer was a worker's delegation token (vxd_). The ceiling the dispatch granted: a service refuses a person-in-the-loop verb when regime is not human.

workspaces.description: "*" (everything already the subject's) or the isolation set; becomes x-user-delegation-workspaces

target.description: the chat's target workspace, a default and never a grant; becomes x-user-delegation-target

Vector.description: A signing test vector: any implementation signing these claims at `now` with `private_key` must produce `token` (Ed25519 signatures are deterministic), and `public_key` is that key's public half. The pair is RFC 8032 section 7.1 TEST 1, a published test key and never a deployment's.

Refusal.description: A refusal vector: verifying `token` with `public_key` at `now` must fail with `reason`. Covers another key, a tampered payload, algorithm confusion (an HMAC keyed with the public key), a missing signature, another scheme and an over-long lifetime.
